feedback: Correct response: penguins live in the south (far away from polar bears); they are flightless birds that swim brilliantly with flipper-wings; Emperors huddle to share warmth and keep the single egg on a parent's feet off the ice.
If a learner agrees with the friend, they may be running on 'bird = flies' and 'cold = North Pole' — re-anchor both: not all birds fly, and penguins are southern animals.
Asking 'what are they brilliant at instead?' should draw out swimming, not just 'they can't fly'.
activities.intendedInsight: A learner who holds the concept relocates penguins to the south, says they are birds that swim rather than fly, and explains huddling and egg-on-feet.
learnerActions: Listen to a friend's claim: 'Penguins live up at the North Pole near the polar bears, and they're birds so of course they can fly.'
Say what is wrong and fix it.
Answer: if a penguin is a bird that can't fly, what is it brilliant at instead?
Explain how Emperor penguins survive the freezing winter.
activities.title: Friend who's half right — correct it
